exposure: maternal BMI (severely obese >35 kg/m2 vs. ≤35 kg/m2)
outcome: composite primary outcome (augmentation, instrumental birth, Caesarean, maternal blood transfusion, 3rd/4th degree tear, maternal admission to higher level care)
cohort: 1122 severely obese (BMI >35 kg/m2) women and 1949 comparison women (BMI ≤35 kg/m2) admitted to alongside midwifery units (AMU) in the United Kingdom between January 1 and December 31, 2016
finding: There was no evidence of significantly increased risk associated with planning birth in an AMU for carefully selected multiparous severely obese women, with BMI 35.1-40kg/m2.
mod_finding: Severely obese nulliparous women were more likely to have an urgent Caesarean section or severe PPH compared with other women admitted to AMUs.
